name: Parc des Princes
note: venues/parc-des-princes.ts: Taillibert's 1972 bowl, 50 curved concrete portiques carrying the roof ring, two tiers of blue seats (the Paris stand's red and white bands), the striped pitch. relation/152838 is building=stadium (height 48) with the pitch's void as its inner ring. front 125 lays local x along the pitch's axis (OSM way/88005247, bearing 35°) with the Paris stand (−z) on the east side. The 24 two-metre ways (87832955…87936909) are the ticket booths and turnstiles round the bowl, which the city drew as little houses with chimneys against the portiques (2026-10-29 bake): removed.

name: Stade Jean-Bouin
note: venues/jean-bouin.ts: Ricciotti's 2013 rugby ground, one skin of pale UHPC lattice pierced with irregular openings over facade and roof, a single steep tier round the pitch, the H posts. relation/6048947 is building=stadium (no height in OSM; ~24 m drawn) with the pitch's void as inner ring. front 187 lays local x along the pitch (way/403524547, bearing 97°).

name: Roland-Garros: Philippe-Chatrier
note: venues/roland-garros.ts: the square bowl of green seats round the clay, cream louvred drum, the retractable roof's two rack rails and its eleven white wings parked at the north end (+x, bearing 21°; the parking end is not confirmed by the sources read). relation/11004030 (building=stadium) carries 304 building:parts, claimed with it. (Named without 'court': render/landmarks.ts skips the footprint for /court/.) The five raised slabs on the south stand (ways 1175316752…993) the bake did not file under the outline are named too.

name: Roland-Garros: Suzanne-Lenglen
note: venues/roland-garros.ts: the round open bowl, green seats, clay court, white piers and a green band round the drum. relation/11004031 (building=stadium, the court its inner ring) with its 186 parts; the other ids are the stands' ground-layer building=roof ways and five raised building:part relations (15897415…563) that the bake keeps as canopy slabs inside the bowl, not as the outline's parts (checked against the 2026-10-29 bake's tiles).

name: Roland-Garros: Simonne-Mathieu
note: venues/roland-garros.ts: Mimram's 2019 court in the Serres d'Auteuil, low stands round the clay walled by four glass greenhouses with the plants against the panes. The real court is sunk ~4 m in the garden; the model cannot dig into the terrain, so it stands at grade. relation/11004029 (building=stadium) and its 468 seat-row parts. Placed by point and size (OSM's outline centre and its 82 x 66 rectangle at bearing 2°): the bake keeps only one of the 468 parts under the dropped outline, and fitted to that hull the court would have come out 41 x 57.

name: Roland-Garros: the outside courts
note: venues/roland-garros.ts COURTS: the clay of courts 2-16 in their white lines, nets and green windbreaks, at their OSM positions (leisure=pitch surface=clay ways 792571216/18/59/60/69/77-80/82-85/160/161) relative to a point 110 m west and 20 m north of this one (COURTS' origin; the entry's own point is on open lawn between courts 6/8 and the Chatrier and its size a token 10 m, so the nonbuildings audit's footprint rectangle does not take in the whole grounds — the builder draws 520 m of courts whatever the size). The city draws those pitches as green pitch areas (no surface in the area kind) - this lays the clay over them. Court 14's round stand is drawn here too; relation/11004024 is its ring. The stand round courts 7 and 9 (relation/11004028, building=yes with the courts as holes, which the city drew as a 28 m block with the clay at the bottom of two wells) is drawn here as a 4.5 m terrace of seats.

name: Accor Arena
note: venues/accor-arena.ts: the POPB's truncated pyramid of lawn, the glass band and Prouvé's dark steel roof frame, the four concrete shafts at the cut corners, DVVD's 2015 glazed hall on the Rue de Bercy (−z, north-east) and the podium on the Boulevard de Bercy (+x). Placed by point and size, not fitted: way/252506849 also holds the parvis and podiums, and its 177 stepped parts are claimed with it. Centre and size from the parts' 19-20 m terrace (177 x 146 in the 51° frame) grown to the slopes' foot.

name: Temple de la Sibylle
note: venues/parks.ts: Davioud's 1869 tholos on the Buttes-Chaumont's rock (after the Temple of Vesta at Tivoli): eight Corinthian columns on a stepped podium, the entablature ring, the low dome. OSM's way is the 5.7 m ring of columns. The cliff and island under it are the terrain's (the DEM), not drawn here.

name: Château de Bagatelle
note: venues/parks.ts: Bélanger's 1777 folly in the Bois de Boulogne, two balustraded storeys of pale stone, the garden front's shallow bow (OSM's ring swells ~3 m out of its north-north-east face, hence front 23) under a low zinc dome, four Tuscan columns on the court front (+z).

name: Rotonde de Chartres
note: venues/parks.ts: Ledoux's 1787 barrière at the Parc Monceau's gate on the Boulevard de Courcelles: sixteen Tuscan columns round the core drum, the upper drum of twelve arched windows, the low zinc dome. relation/3066029 (height 20, heritage 2), 15 m across.

name: Parc André-Citroën: the north greenhouse
note: venues/parks.ts citroenGreenhouse: Patrick Berger's 1992 glass nave at the head of the lawn, 45 x 15 m, 15 m to the eaves, the mullion grid, the plants against the lower panes, a glass ridge roof. front 30 lays the long axis (bearing 120) along x, the +x gable to the lawn and the Seine (north-west).

name: Parc André-Citroën: the south greenhouse
note: venues/parks.ts citroenGreenhouse, its twin across the water jets' peristyle (OSM way/163863438).

name: Le Pré Catelan
note: The Napoleon III pavilion (1856) in the Bois de Boulogne's Pré Catelan, now Lenôtre's restaurant: two storeys of tall windows in pale stone under a slate roof - a restyle, its silhouette is OSM's (way/83115461, 45 x 58).

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie J5
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.J5: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Rond-point des Canaux J5): open frame under a red roof slab (OSM building=roof, wall=no), the walkway to the canal bridge. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L1
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L1: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Éclat de Folie L1): the north entrance (Avenue Corentin-Cariou), a canopy wing to the gate. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L2
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L2: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie L2): the bar-restaurant: the glazed round annex OSM maps west of the cube, a quarter wheel. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L3
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L3: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie de l’Écluse L3): by the Canal Saint-Denis lock, a straight stair up its face. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L4
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L4: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Kiosque à Musique L4): the bandstand (kiosque): open frame, canopy wings both sides. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L5
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L5: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie des visites L5): the spiral stair in its drum and the low glazed annex OSM maps south of the cube (OSM's 49 m tail along the canal is not drawn). Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L6
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L6: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie des Vents et des Dunes L6): the airlock to the Jardin des vents et des dunes, a walkway out of the frame. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L7
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L7: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Atelier des visites L7): a lift tower over the roof. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L8
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L8: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie du Théâtre L8): by the Théâtre Paris-Villette, a quarter wheel. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie L9
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.L9: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie information Villette L9): information and ticketing at the Porte de Pantin, the cube with its glazed annex (OSM way 27 × 17 m). Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N1
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N1: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Horloge N1): the clock folie: the white dial on its north-west face, a mast. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N4
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N4: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Observatoire N4): the observatory: open upper floors, a mast, a stair. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N5
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N5: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie du Canal N5): the spiral stair drum OSM maps at its north corner. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N6
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N6: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie des Fêtes N6): the round stair drum OSM maps at its west corner. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N7
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N7: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie douce N7): a quarter wheel; the porch roof OSM maps west of it. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N8
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N8: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Janvier N8): the Folie Janvier (offices), a lift tower. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie N9
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.N9: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Cité de la Musique N9): the entrance to the Cité de la musique, a canopy wing. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie P4
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.P4: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Argonaute P4): beside the Argonaute submarine, a straight stair. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie P5
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.P5: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Ateliers du Parc P5): the terrace over the Canal de l'Ourcq: the stair drum OSM maps, a walkway. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie P6
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.P6: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Belvédère P6): the belvedere: an open top floor, a stair up its face. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie P7
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.P7: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Café P7): the café, its 2012 glazed extension (OSM's wedge south of the cube, drawn as a box). Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie P8
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.P8: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie Musique P8): by the Philharmonie, the canopy on posts OSM maps east of the cube. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie R4
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.R4: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie escalier R4): the walkways the Galerie de la Villette runs through, a stair. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie R5
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.R5: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie échangeur R5): the échangeur where the galerie meets the east footbridge: two walkways. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Parc de la Villette: Folie R6
note: venues/villette.ts FOLIE.R6: Tschumi's red 10.8 m cube of 3 × 3 × 3 cells (Folie billetterie du Zénith R6): the Zénith ticket office, the stair drum OSM maps. Placed by point on the cube's centre and turned to the 120 m grid (front 233.7), see the file's header.

name: Grande Halle de la Villette
note: venues/villette.ts: Mérindol's cattle hall of 1867 (245 × 85 × 19 m, Wikipedia fr): the open colonnade of white cast-iron columns and fanned brackets round the ground floor under the overhanging eaves, the glazed aisles, the clerestory nave under its low gable, the glass gables, the clock on the Porte de Pantin end (front 144, the SE gable). way/63971649 (241 × 86 m, height 16 + roof 10 in OSM).

name: Jardin des Plantes: the Grandes Serres
note: venues/serres.ts: one model over the row of glasshouses on the garden's south side (local x along bearing 70, the garden at −z): Rohault de Fleury's two square pavilions of 1834–36 (the Serre des déserts, way/1288442711, and the Serre de Nouvelle-Calédonie, part way/1476752442) on their stone terrace with the ramp between, dark green iron and purple-cast panes under curved roofs and railed lanterns; Berger's 1937 Jardin d'hiver (part way/320012507) with its whitewashed glass, bracketed eaves, curved roof and lantern and the lean-to on its front; the low curved gallery to the west (way/23758088). Placed by point (the five ways' common frame) rather than fitted: the outline way/23758079 holds both the east pavilion and the winter garden. Positions from the OSM rings turned into that frame.

name: Jardin du Luxembourg: the Grand Bassin and the terraces
note: venues/gardens.ts: the elongated octagon of the Grand Bassin (OSM way/4294027, its long sides north-south) brim-full under a stone coping, the centre basin with the children holding up the vasque and its jet, the toy sailboats, the green chairs round it; and the balustraded terrace walls round the sunken parterre from OSM's barrier=wall ways 194193439-442 and 454094953-955 (gapped at the stairs), a Queen of France on her pedestal every ~16 m. The parterre really lies ~2 m under the terraces; the DEM's ground cannot be dug, so the walls stand on it. Placed by point at the octagon's centre, front 182 (+x east, +z to the palace); size is the basin's, which is all the tree clearing should take.

name: Jardin des Tuileries: the Grand Bassin Rond
note: venues/gardens.ts: the round basin at the Louvre end of the garden's axis (OSM way/14037695, 40 m), its coping and its water at the brim (the city's own water lies 2.5 m down in a pit, region riverDrop), the central jet and its ring of spouts, the green chairs. Placed by point at its centre.

name: Jardin des Tuileries: the Grand Bassin Octogonal
note: venues/gardens.ts: the octagonal basin at the Concorde end between the ramps (OSM way/54188993, 68 m, sides 26.1 m square to the axis at bearing 116), coping, brim-full water, the jet, the green chairs. Placed by point at its centre, front 206 so local x runs along the axis.

name: Jardin des Tuileries: La Terrasse de Pomone
note: venues/gardens.ts tuileriesKiosk: the café kiosk north of the Grand Couvert's west side (OSM node 1679239832 names it): a small square pavilion of green-painted timber and glass under a hipped zinc roof and lantern, its terrace of tables under terracotta parasols round it (Commons, 'La Terrasse de Pomone brasserie.jpg'). Fitted to the OSM way.

name: Jardin des Tuileries: Petit Plisson
note: venues/gardens.ts tuileriesKiosk: the café kiosk in the northern Grand Couvert (OSM node 1686623823): a small square pavilion of green-painted timber and glass under a hipped zinc roof and lantern, its terrace of tables under terracotta parasols round it (Commons, 'La Terrasse de Pomone brasserie.jpg'). Fitted to the OSM way.

name: Jardin des Tuileries: Café des Marronniers
note: venues/gardens.ts tuileriesKiosk: the café kiosk under the chestnuts by the Orangerie (OSM names the way): a small square pavilion of green-painted timber and glass under a hipped zinc roof and lantern, its terrace of tables under terracotta parasols round it (Commons, 'La Terrasse de Pomone brasserie.jpg'). Fitted to the OSM way.

name: Jardin des Tuileries: the café kiosk by the Feuillants
note: venues/gardens.ts tuileriesKiosk: the café pavilion at the Feuillants terrace's foot (OSM disused:amenity=cafe, 16 × 20 m): a small square pavilion of green-painted timber and glass under a hipped zinc roof and lantern, its terrace of tables under terracotta parasols round it (Commons, 'La Terrasse de Pomone brasserie.jpg'). Fitted to the OSM way.

name: Parc Monceau: the Naumachie
note: venues/gardens.ts: the oval basin at the north-east end of the park's stream (the oval head of OSM's water way/55761392, ~50 x 34 m, long axis bearing 71 = local x), its coping open to the stream at the south-west, and round its far side the colonnade of fluted Corinthian columns from the Valois rotunda at Saint-Denis: 24 columns on a 210-degree arc 2.4 m back from the brim, the entablature on three runs, two broken shafts. The colonnade is not in OSM: its arc and count are from the photographs (Commons PH82662, A39089S). The stream's water is the city's (2.5 m down); no pool is drawn here, the oval being open to it.

name: Jardin du Luxembourg: the Kiosque à musique
note: venues/gardens.ts: the round bandstand in the garden's east side (OSM way/62848443, 12.5 m, leisure=bandstand): a stone base and steps, sixteen slender iron columns with brackets, a railing, the concave zinc roof, lantern and finial. Fitted to its way.

name: Orangerie du Luxembourg
note: The Orangerie du Sénat (1839, Gisors) on the garden's west side: one tall storey of round-headed windows to the south under a slate roof, where the orange trees winter - a restyle, its silhouette is OSM's (way/62848404, 74 x 18 m).

name: Buttes-Chaumont: the suspension bridge
note: venues/buttes-bridges.ts: the 63 m footbridge to the island (OSM way/45777307, bridge:structure=suspension, from (3678, 2285) to (3616, 2282) local): the timber deck between red mesh railings and a polished steel handrail, the flat lattice chains swooping from a pair of faux-rock pylons at each end, the hangers and back-stays (Commons, 'Passerelle suspendue Buttes Chaumont Paris 19e.jpg'). Placed by point at its middle, front 357 so local x runs along it (the island, east, at -x); the deck runs from the ground at one end to the ground at the other with a slight sag. coversRaised: it is the bridge way's own deck.

name: Buttes-Chaumont: the Pont des Suicides bridge
note: venues/buttes-bridges.ts: the brick arch to the island from the south (OSM way/29266078, 22 m): a 13 m brick barrel under a ring of stone voussoirs, the spandrels and abutments down into the gorge, a stone cornice and the red cast-iron lattice parapets on stone dies (Commons, 'Paris - Buttes Chaumont - Pont des suicidés 01.jpg'). Placed by point, front 90 so local x runs north along it (the island at +x); the deck at the higher bank's ground. ('bridge' in the name keeps the span rectangle from clearing the trees under it.)

name: Hippodrome de Longchamp: the grandstand
note: venues/racecourses.ts: Dominique Perrault's 2018 stand (the '160 mètres' of Wikipedia fr): thin white trays stacked over the track, each floor reaching further out than the one below, bronze soffits and glass balustrades on the lips, terracotta seats on the low rake in front, yellow stair cores through the stack, the glazed panoramic box on top cantilevered 14 m past the north end, bronze louvres on the back to the Route des Tribunes (Commons: Perrault's own photographs). way/584395763 (152 x 30 m along bearing 21); the track's outer ring passes just east of it, so front 111 and the cantilever at local +x (north, as in the photograph from the track). No height in OSM: ~26 m from the photographs' five levels.

name: Hippodrome d'Auteuil: the north stand
note: venues/racecourses.ts auteuilStand: one of the four stands in a row along bearing 25 facing the steeplechase course (front 296): the 1924 tribunes (Wikipedia fr), an arcade of round arches under the lower tier of seats, the upper deck and its rake under a cantilevered concrete canopy on square piers, the taller stair pavilions at the ends (Commons, 'Tribune hippodrome d'Auteuil - panoramio.jpg'). Fitted to way/83202275. Which of the row is which stand, and whether all four are of 1924, is not settled by the sources read.

name: Hippodrome d'Auteuil: the second stand
note: venues/racecourses.ts auteuilStand: one of the four stands in a row along bearing 25 facing the steeplechase course (front 296): the 1924 tribunes (Wikipedia fr), an arcade of round arches under the lower tier of seats, the upper deck and its rake under a cantilevered concrete canopy on square piers, the taller stair pavilions at the ends (Commons, 'Tribune hippodrome d'Auteuil - panoramio.jpg'). Fitted to way/83202264. Which of the row is which stand, and whether all four are of 1924, is not settled by the sources read.

name: Hippodrome d'Auteuil: the third stand
note: venues/racecourses.ts auteuilStand: one of the four stands in a row along bearing 25 facing the steeplechase course (front 296): the 1924 tribunes (Wikipedia fr), an arcade of round arches under the lower tier of seats, the upper deck and its rake under a cantilevered concrete canopy on square piers, the taller stair pavilions at the ends (Commons, 'Tribune hippodrome d'Auteuil - panoramio.jpg'). Fitted to way/83202316. Which of the row is which stand, and whether all four are of 1924, is not settled by the sources read.

name: Hippodrome d'Auteuil: the south stand
note: venues/racecourses.ts auteuilStand: one of the four stands in a row along bearing 25 facing the steeplechase course (front 296): the 1924 tribunes (Wikipedia fr), an arcade of round arches under the lower tier of seats, the upper deck and its rake under a cantilevered concrete canopy on square piers, the taller stair pavilions at the ends (Commons, 'Tribune hippodrome d'Auteuil - panoramio.jpg'). Fitted to way/83202288. Which of the row is which stand, and whether all four are of 1924, is not settled by the sources read.

name: Jardin d'Acclimatation: the Porte des Sablons
note: venues/acclimatation.ts: the garden's main entrance on the Avenue du Mahatma-Gandhi (OSM node 128407713, barrier=entrance, entrance=main): the two little white lodges with gabled slate roofs and round gable windows at the ends (ways 1084917461 and 1084917464, 35.8 m apart), the two glazed ticket booths under broad shallow iron roofs between them (ways 1084917462-463), the green railings and lamps (Commons, 'Entrée Jardin d'Acclimatation.jpg'). Placed by point midway between the lodges, local x along their line (bearing 25), the avenue at -z (front 115); the four ways are claimed. The garden's pavilions (the Palais d'Hiver, the Grande Volière) are not drawn.

name: Hippodrome de Longchamp: the low buildings behind the grandstand
note: The 313 m L-shaped way behind and north of Perrault's stand (no height or name in OSM), which the city drew as a seven-storey Haussmann block with chimneys in the middle of the Bois (2026-10-30 shot). Held to two storeys under a flat roof; what it is (the stand's podium, the weighing room, the paddock buildings) is not settled by the sources read.

name: Hippodrome de Longchamp: the 1904 stands
note: The two long ways just south-west of Perrault's stand along the same line (140 and 81 m, no height in OSM), likely the stone stands of 1904 that Wikipedia fr says were kept and moved south-west of the course; the city drew them as seven-storey apartment blocks (2026-10-30 shot). Held to three storeys of stone under a flat roof until they are modelled.

name: Enclos Saint-Lazare: the palm garden
note: The garden behind the Médiathèque Françoise-Sagan: a zigzag path between raised beds under windmill palms (owner's street view, 2026-10-30). OSM maps only a paved court.

name: Stade Pierre-de-Coubertin
note: venues/coubertin.ts: the 1937 hall (rebuilt 1946, renovated 1990; Wikipedia fr) at the Porte de Saint-Cloud. A rider on the Avenue Georges Lafont sees a giant order of red brick piers against cream wall under a deep concrete eave, with the 1990 silver stair drums and glass between the piers (Commons, Stade Pierre de Coubertin, November 2016). Height estimated from the photographs; the drums' places are inferred from the plan's notches.

name: Halle Georges-Carpentier
note: venues/carpentier.ts: the Palais des sports de la Porte d'Ivry of 1960, renovated and renamed 1988 (Wikipedia fr). From the Boulevard Masséna: a white base, pale ribbed panels between dark blue posts rising to a shallow gable, red brick entrance blocks at the ends (Commons, Halle Carpentier - Face avant, Entrée du public, F8495). Heights estimated from the photographs.

name: Dôme de Paris - Palais des Sports
note: venues/dome-paris.ts: Dufau and de Larivière on Buckminster Fuller's geodesic process, 1959-60; about 70 m across, 1,100 aluminium panels (Wikipedia fr). A shallow geodesic cap of dished triangular panels over low corrugated annexes on OSM's outline, the blue boards to the Place de la Porte de Versailles (Commons, DÔME de Paris; Dôme de Paris (Palais des Sports) façade). Height and roof height OSM's. Placed by point so the dome stands on its own centre, not the middle of its parts' hull.

name: Stade Sébastien-Charléty
note: venues/charlety.ts: Henri and Bruno Gaudin, 1991-94, 19,151 seats, the blue track of 2019-20 (Wikipedia fr). OSM maps only the grounds (way/663183242), the pitch and the track, so this is a point on the track's middle, turned to the pitch's long edges; 220 x 184 m is the room the grounds leave. The rider sees a pale ring of concrete fins with four tall white masts, thin long roofs over the high long sides, white sails at the corners (Commons, Paris Stade Sébastien Charléty; Stade Charléty 145, 230, 700). Heights estimated from the photographs.

name: Plenitude Arena
note: venues/plenitude-arena.ts: Christian de Portzamparc, 2013-17, the Paris La Défense Arena; 592 aluminium-and-glass scales, a fixed roof (Wikipedia fr). From the Jardins de l'Arche: a great rounded block in overlapping pale scales over a glazed ground floor, the dark screen in its white frame, the green name (Commons, Entrée 4 Paris Défense Arena; Enseignes Naming Plenitude Arena). Height and roof height OSM's; the 11-level wing is way/443073294, the Conseil départemental's. The scale's outline and the screen's place are read from the photographs.

name: Piscine Molitor
note: venues/molitor.ts: Lucien Pollet, 1929, rebuilt and reopened 2014, its outdoor pool 46 m (Wikipedia fr). Yellow walls with dark bands and the name at the door on Rue Nungesser-et-Coli (Commons, Hôtel Piscine Molitor); from above the summer pool in three tiers of white railings and blue cabin doors, OSM's courtyard; the winter pool's glass roof to the east. Heights estimated from the photographs; the glass roof's outline is an estimate from the plan.

name: Piscine Georges-Vallerey
note: venues/vallerey.ts: the Piscine des Tourelles of the 1924 Olympics, Roger Taillibert's renovation of 1986-89, redone 2024 (Wikipedia fr). From the Avenue Gambetta: the end of a glass barrel vault with a pale rim over beige masses, the glazed bay between two great round columns, the name, the pale green tower with a round window (Commons, Piscine Georges Vallerey 8 April 2017 and 2024-11-01). Vault width and heights estimated from the photographs.

name: La Seine Musicale
note: venues/seine-musicale.ts: Shigeru Ban and Jean de Gastines, 2017: the auditorium's egg of braided wood under moving solar sails, the Grande Seine, the Jardin Bellini on its roof (Wikipedia fr). From the bridges and the Meudon bank: a long white ship on the point of the Île Seguin, the great lawn, the egg and the tall sail in front of it (Commons, La Seine musicale at night, (64634), (84847)). The plan is OSM's; heights and the sail's outline are estimated from the photographs; the sail is drawn to the south.

name: Palais des Congrès
note: venues/palais-congres.ts: the 1974 block (Gillet, Maloletenkov, Betin, Guibout) with Christian de Portzamparc's 1999 inclined facade and the Bordeaux amphitheatre's inverted cone showing on it (Wikipedia fr; Commons, L'escalier du Palais des Congrés à Paris). The plan and the 21 and 40 m heights are OSM's; the plane's foot, its glazing and the cone's place on it are from memory, no elevation having been found. The Hyatt tower is its own building and stays.

name: Le Cent Quatre
note: venues/cent-quatre.ts: the old municipal undertakers', its inscription over the arch (Commons, Le Centquatre, les anciennes pompes funèbres de Paris). The glass-roofed iron halls and the stone gable striped with brick, its fan-headed window and oculi (Commons, Le Cent Quatre à Paris, juin 2012); stone ranges on both streets. Courts are OSM's; the halls' sections and range heights estimated from the photographs.
